Types

ClosureRoot = object
  name*: string
  constraint*: VersionConstraint
  features*: seq[string]
  url*: string
  refStr*: string
One direct dependency of a root package that this kit does not own (a local project whose manifest lives in the working tree, say). Passing these to installPackage installs the whole closure in a single resolution pass instead of one pass per direct dep — the whole point, since each pass redoes discovery, resolution, record writes and pruning. 
UpdateItem = tuple[name, oldVer, newVer: string]
One package moved by an update: name plus installed version before and after. Callers (e.g. clue update inside a project) use this to rewrite version constraints in the project manifest.

    ReadDirEffect, RootEffect, WriteIOEffect, WriteDirEffect, ReadIOEffect,

The real package name a repository URL provides.

Resolution order: registry → cloned manifest → basename guess. The manifest is authoritative: a private or newly-published repo absent from the registry still yields its true name once cloned, and a stale registry entry is corrected by what is actually on disk. When the canonical name differs, the _cache/<guessed> checkout is moved to _cache/<canonical> (when the latter is absent) so later phases (discoverVersions, getDeps, install) find it under one identity.

Registry-aware dependency name. A URL-only dependency (no name) is looked up in the registry first, so a repository whose basename differs from its package (supranim/tasks → supranim_tasks) resolves to the real name. Falls back to the repository basename for private or unpublished URLs; callers then refine via canonicalNameForUrl which reads the cloned manifest (the ultimate authority).

Generic install via cfg. Returns true on success. buildHook is opt-in (builder stays in clue). When depsOnly is true the requested package itself is skipped (no files, no record, no build) and only its dependency closure is installed; the root's direct deps are recorded as roots so pruning keeps them. When directRoots is non-empty the whole closure of those dependencies is resolved and installed in one pass. pkgName is then only a label: it is never resolved against the registry, cloned, installed or recorded.

Pool worker: announces the start through the progress channel (replayed on the caller's thread post-join, resolved from the caller's own jobs via idx per the pool.nim contract), then checks out and copies. Finish lines are printed in bulk by the caller under a Resolved packages: header (deterministic order). Worker-safe: raw filesystem/git only — no cfg, no DB, no callbacks.

Root metadata lookup: the requested source (or the default source) first, then any known source. The fallback covers packages that live in no configured registry source — e.g. direct rows recorded for locally- or URL-installed packages — so dependents resolve without --source. Develop-mode checkouts still win outright inside fetchPkgMeta.

Check-then-update over an explicit package list in a single process.

The version check (discoverVersionsBatch with refresh = true) is the multithreaded phase: clones/fetches run on the install-time pool while DB writes stay sequential on this thread. Entries already at their latest version are skipped silently, so up-to-date packages print nothing. Only outdated entries are installed (sequentially, the store is not thread-safe), with one header and one summary for the whole run and deduped clone-start lines for shared transitive deps. Returns the packages that were actually reinstalled with their before/after versions.
